data.cultural_impact: In Islamic culture, asking for forgiveness is a vital aspect of building and maintaining relationships, whether it is between individuals or between the individual and God. The name "Tawab" is a constant reminder of the significance of seeking and granting forgiveness. This value is celebrated and encouraged in various aspects of Islamic life, from daily prayers to community gatherings and beyond.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Tawab" holds great significance as it represents the journey towards self-improvement and redemption. It serves as a reminder that no matter how many mistakes one may make in life, there is always an opportunity to ask for forgiveness and start anew. The spiritual power of this name lies in its potential to inspire repentance, humility, and a renewed commitment to living a virtuous life in the sight of God.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah (Vol. 9, p. 181) The name Tawab carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.time_period: During the period of the Rightly-Guided Caliphs
historical_references.context: Ibn 'Abbas (R) said: 'I heard the Prophet (S) say, 'The repentant (Tawab) will enter Paradise before the constant believer (Sadiq).' [The Prophet (S) then added,] 'Have I not guaranteed it for you?' The people were pleased with that. Later, when 'Umar ibn Al-Khattab (R) became the caliph, the people who had committed major sins asked for his permission to repent. He gave them permission, and when they repented, he gave them the title 'Al-Tawabun' (the Repentant).

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Qurtubi's Al-Jami' li Ahkam Al-Qur'an (Vol. 2, p. 391) The name Tawab carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.time_period: During the period of the Umayyad Caliphate
historical_references.context: Al-Qurtubi mentioned in his commentary on Surah Al-An'am (6:54) that the people who had committed major sins during the time of 'Umar ibn Al-Khattab (R) repented and sought forgiveness from him, so he gave them the title 'Al-Tawabun' (the Repentant). Later, this title was given to a group of people during the Umayyad Caliphate who committed major sins and repented, seeking forgiveness from 'Umar ibn 'Abd Al-Aziz (R).

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Tawab in the Islamic tradition stands for a person who seeks repentance and forgiveness from Allah. In the modern context, this concept is increasingly embraced on various platforms. On social media, hashtags such as #Tawab and #ForForgiveness are used by individuals to express their desire for spiritual growth and seeking Allah's forgiveness. Educational apps, such as SeekersHub and Quran.com, offer resources for individuals to learn about the Islamic teachings on repentance and seek guidance from scholars. In mental health communities, Tawab is recognized as an essential aspect of mental and emotional wellbeing and is discussed as a means to promote self-forgiveness and healing.
